items.stem: A compliance team asks an architect to commit a fraud-triage model to "95% accuracy" before the next audit, without stating whether a missed case or a false alarm costs more. What should happen before a threshold is set?

opts.t: Return to discovery and price both error directions before setting any threshold.
Bias the model toward recall and route every flagged case to human review.
Commit to the 95% target, since both error directions are likely low-cost and easily corrected.
Benchmark several candidate models against the 95% figure to find the one that reaches it most reliably.

items.whyRight: The sponsor has stated a number but not which error direction costs more; a flat accuracy target cannot encode that asymmetry, so pricing both directions and letting the ratio set the threshold and review placement comes before any commitment is made.

whyWrong.B: Biasing toward recall is correct once the asymmetry is known and priced; here neither direction's cost has been established, so the direction chosen is a guess.
whyWrong.C: The stem states the costs are unstated, not that they are low; assuming both directions are cheap contradicts what the compliance team actually said.
whyWrong.D: A benchmark produces a number before there is a target error cost to interpret it against, the same gap a bare accuracy figure already has.

items.t1Clause: without stating whether a missed case or a false alarm costs more
items.factAnswerRaw: Return to discovery and price both directions

items.stem: A product lead confirms the disputed-claims segment carries no regulator attestation requirement, yet a fifth of cases still route to a reviewer even as model accuracy keeps improving. What should the architect tell them?

opts.t: Explain that AI systems are probabilistic and human review remains a safety best practice for this segment.
Say the system cannot verify its own output against ground truth, and that better evaluation data could close it.
Commit to removing the reviewer once accuracy on this segment crosses a stated threshold.
Refuse to remove the reviewer, citing the segment's regulatory attestation requirement, and quantify what the segment is worth.

items.whyRight: The segment's limit is that the system cannot verify its own output against ground truth, not a missing attestation; naming that distinction points to the actual remedy, richer evaluation data, instead of a generic caution or a false regulatory citation.

whyWrong.A: This is true of AI systems generally but names nothing specific; the stakeholder still cannot tell whether this segment is closable or a standing limit.
whyWrong.C: Accuracy improving is not the same as having verified ground truth; committing to a threshold promises a guarantee the missing evaluation data does not yet support.
whyWrong.D: The stem states no regulator attestation applies to this segment; citing one as the reason for keeping the reviewer contradicts the fact already given.

items.factAnswerRaw: Say so: the system cannot check its own output on these cases against ground truth

items.stem: A support team has logged the input, the output, and a reviewer's note for every user-reported failure in a shared tracker for six months, but the pre-release evaluation set has not grown since launch. What does this represent?

opts.t: A working feedback loop, since every case already carries an input, an output, and a reviewer's note.
Restructure this as a loop that captures input, output, expected output, and reviewer, then feeds the evaluation set.
Sufficient, because a named product owner already reviews the tracker weekly and can act on trends.
A broken loop: the system stays measured against an evaluation set that diverges further from production inputs every week.

items.whyRight: The tracker already captures each case's input, output, and reviewer note, so the defect is not structural; the loop is broken because none of that captured detail is feeding the evaluation set, which keeps aging against a population the system no longer sees.

whyWrong.A: The stem states the evaluation set has not grown since launch; calling the arrangement working directly contradicts that stated fact.
whyWrong.B: That rebuild is the fix when nothing is being captured yet; here input, output, and reviewer notes already exist, and the missing link is the feed to the evaluation set.
whyWrong.C: A weekly review of the tracker is not the same mechanism as growing the evaluation set; the two remain disconnected regardless of how often anyone reads the tracker.

items.t1Clause: has logged the input, the output, and a reviewer's note for every user-reported failure in a shared tracker

items.stem: Nine months after a document-extraction pipeline shipped, a team weighs replacing the model with a larger-context version; the only record is a component diagram and inventory, and the latency budget is unchanged. What should they check first?

opts.t: Check whether the alternatives, trade-offs, and constraint behind the model choice were ever recorded at all.
Check the recorded latency ceiling that drove the original choice, and re-evaluate the decision against it.
Commission a more detailed component diagram and an updated service inventory before deciding.
Ship the larger-context model now, and audit a sample of outputs after the change to confirm nothing broke.

items.whyRight: A diagram and an inventory show what the system is, not why the model tier was chosen; before swapping it, the team needs to know whether the alternatives, trade-offs, and constraint behind that choice were ever written down.

whyWrong.B: Nothing in the record shows a latency ceiling was ever captured; there is no recorded constraint for this option to check against.
whyWrong.C: More detail in the diagram and inventory still describes what the system is; it does not supply the missing reasoning behind the original choice.
whyWrong.D: Shipping first and auditing outputs afterward risks a regression the missing rationale might have flagged in advance, on a change already worth pausing to check.

items.t1Clause: the only record is a component diagram and inventory
